headline: Bayesian models infer dengue and malaria transmission from genomic and surveillance data
label: Bayesian Inference For Transmission Dynamics
summary: Recent preprints and publications pair simulation-trained and ensemble inference with pathogen genomics to resolve transmission dynamics.
synthesis: The dominant thread is Bayesian inference of latent transmission or kinetic states from partially observed data. Plasmotrack infers directed transmission networks from polyclonal P. falciparum infections, and DENcode couples epidemiological and haplotype-based genetic kernels to estimate dengue transmission probability. M-SDT fits a mechanistic seasonal compartmental dengue model to 2020–2024 Ahmedabad zone data with bootstrap uncertainty and intervention scenarios. On the methods side, eSMC2 replaces SMC2's inner particle filter with an EnKF to speed state-parameter inference, tested on mpox incidence. A BayesFlow neural posterior estimation workflow, trained on simulations, applies similar logic to host kinetics, integrating bulk and spatial imaging to infer viral and interferon responses in airway epithelium. What is new is the coupling of genetic relatedness with epidemiological kernels and the reduction of inferential cost through ensemble or simulation-trained estimators.
